intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m. Trek through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and glacial moraines while enjoying breathtaking views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks. The trail passes through traditional Gurung villages offering authentic cultural immersion alongside stunning Himalayan scenery.
experiences.location: Annapurna Sanctuary, Chhomrong to ABC Trail, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises in Nepal. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges including over a dozen peaks above 7,000m. The 2-hour ascent from Ghorepani is manageable for most fitness levels and rewards trekkers with a 180-degree panoramic view.
experiences.location: Poon Hill, Ghorepani, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering solitude and raw Himalayan beauty away from crowded routes. Trek through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests to high-altitude meadows with unobstructed close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain) and Mardi Himal peak. Encounter diverse wildlife including Himalayan tahr and red pandas along this pristine trail.
experiences.location: Mardi Himal Trail, Low Camp to High Camp, Eastern Annapurna

experiences.name: Traditional Gurung Village Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Explore the traditional Gurung and Magar villages of Ghandruk, one of the largest Gurung settlements in Nepal. Visit the Gurung Museum to learn about indigenous culture, customs, and history. Interact with locals, observe traditional stone-paved pathways, and enjoy authentic dal bhat and local millet raksi (spirit) while learning about the Gurkha warrior heritage of this mountain community.
experiences.location: Ghandruk Village, Modi Khola Valley, Southern Annapurna

experiences.name: Jhinu Danda Natural Hot Springs Soak
experiences.description: Reward tired trekking muscles with a rejuvenating soak in the natural hot springs along the Modi Khola river at Jhinu Danda. These geothermal pools sit at around 1,780m elevation surrounded by lush subtropical forest and the sound of rushing glacial waters. The mineral-rich waters are believed to have therapeutic properties and provide the perfect recovery experience after days of high-altitude trekking.
experiences.location: Jhinu Danda Hot Springs, Modi Khola River, New Bridge Area, Annapurna

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00. Clear immigration and collect baggage. Exchange currency at the airport (better rates available in Thamel). Take a local bus or shared taxi to Thamel (budget option: ~NPR 200-300). Check in to a budget guesthouse in Thamel and rest. Begin permit arrangements: visit the Nepal Tourism Board office to obtain ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) and TIMS card (approx. USD 30-40 total). Stroll around Thamel to get oriented, pick up any last-minute trekking supplies from local gear shops.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through the lively streets of Thamel. Visit Kathmandu Durbar Square (short tuk-tuk ride, entry ~NPR 1000 for foreigners) for a quick cultural introduction. Return to Thamel for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eaten on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport — dal bhat or momo from an airport café (~NPR 300)
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a light snack in Thamel upon arrival — try a local bakery sandwich or samosa (~NPR 150-200)
meals.dinner: Dinner at OR2K or a local Nepali restaurant in Thamel — dal bhat set meal (~NPR 400-600). Budget-friendly and filling.

day_by_day.notes: Prioritize getting ACAP and TIMS permits today or first thing tomorrow morning — offices close by 5 PM. Keep hydrated and rest well for the trek ahead. Budget guesthouses in Thamel cost NPR 600-1200 per night.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Pashupatinath Temple and Boudhanath Stupa — two of Kathmandu's most iconic spiritual sites. Entry to Boudhanath ~NPR 400. Circumambulate the stupa with locals and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere. Grab a light breakfast at a café near Boudhanath.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the bus station (Prithvi Highway Bus Park) and board a local tourist bus or public bus to Pokhara (~8 hours, NPR 500-800). The scenic drive through the hills and along the Trishuli River is beautiful. Settle in and enjoy the views.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Pokhara by evening. Check in to a budget guesthouse on Lakeside (Baidam) — rooms from NPR 600-1000/night. Take a short walk along Phewa Lake to stretch your legs after the long bus ride.

meals.breakfast: Café near Boudhanath — eggs on toast and tea (~NPR 250-350)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or buy dal bhat at a roadside dhaba along the Pokhara highway (~NPR 200-300)
meals.dinner: Lakeside restaurant in Pokhara — try Nepali thali or pasta at a budget eatery (~NPR 400-600)

day_by_day.notes: Book the bus ticket the night before from a Thamel travel agent to secure a seat. Carry snacks and water for the bus journey. Pokhara is the gateway to the Annapurna Circuit and base for all trekking permits.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for sunrise views of the Annapurna and Machapuchare (Fishtail) peaks from the Pokhara lakeside. Rent a rowboat on Phewa Lake (~NPR 400/hour) and paddle to the Tal Barahi Temple on an island in the middle of the lake. Enjoy the reflections of the Himalayas on the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (entry ~NPR 400) — excellent exhibits on Himalayan geography, climbing history, and local cultures. Afterward, head to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for panoramic views of Pokhara Valley and the Annapurna range — hike up (~45 min) or take a short taxi ride.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Lakeside Bazaar. Visit a gear rental shop to rent any missing trekking equipment (trekking poles, sleeping bag, down jacket — rental ~NPR 100-300/day each). Prepare your pack for the trek starting tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Lakeside café — porridge with honey and banana, tea (~NPR 250-350)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near the Mountain Museum — momo plate and lassi (~NPR 350-450)
meals.dinner: Lakeside restaurant — pizza or dal bhat at a budget spot (~NPR 400-600). Try the local Pokhara specialty: Newari cuisine if available.

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season in Nepal — weather is typically clear and dry, ideal for mountain views. Confirm your ACAP and TIMS permits are in order before heading to the trailhead. Pack light — budget teahouses along the route provide bedding.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early local bus or shared jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (1.5-2 hours, ~NPR 200-300). Begin the trek from Nayapul — a classic entry point to the Annapurna Sanctuary and Poon Hill routes. Trek through Modi Khola valley, passing terraced fields, suspension bridges, and small villages. Reach Tikhedhunga (1,540m) after approximately 3-4 hours of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking uphill from Tikhedhunga through a famous stone staircase to Ulleri (1,960m) — a steep but rewarding climb of about 1.5-2 hours. Arrive at Ulleri and rest at a teahouse. Enjoy views of the Annapurna South and Hiunchuli peaks. Explore the small Magar village.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a teahouse in Ulleri (~NPR 200-400/night, room often free or discounted if you eat meals there). Socialize with other trekkers. Enjoy the cool mountain air and stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast in Pokhara before departure — egg and chapati (~NPR 200)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga (~NPR 400-500)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or noodle soup at Ulleri teahouse (~NPR 400-500)

day_by_day.notes: The climb from Tikhedhunga to Ulleri involves over 3,000 stone steps — take it slow, stay hydrated, and use trekking poles if available. This is the Ghorepani-Poon Hill route, one of the most popular and budget-friendly treks in the Annapurna region.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning trek from Ulleri through rhododendron and oak forests. The trail gradually ascends through beautiful forest cover. Arrive at Ghorepani (2,860m) after approximately 3-4 hours. Check in to a teahouse and drop your bags. Immediately hike up to Poon Hill (3,210m) — a 45-minute steep climb — for stunning 360-degree panoramic views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, Machapuchare, and dozens of other Himalayan peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for a late lunch. Rest and acclimatize. Explore the small village and interact with local Magar and Gurung communities. Visit the small local monastery if open.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset views from Ghorepani village. The Annapurna range glows golden at dusk. Warm up by the teahouse fire with fellow trekkers. Share stories and plan the next day.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Ulleri teahouse (~NPR 300-400)
meals.lunch: Fried rice or noodle soup at Ghorepani (~NPR 400-500)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with vegetable curry at Ghorepani teahouse (~NPR 450-550)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill at sunrise is even more spectacular — consider waking at 4:30 AM tomorrow for the sunrise hike (entry fee ~NPR 100). October skies are usually crystal clear. Ghorepani has multiple teahouses — negotiate for a free room if you commit to eating all meals there.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 4:30 AM and hike to Poon Hill for the iconic Himalayan sunrise — one of the most breathtaking experiences in Nepal. Watch the peaks turn from deep purple to fiery orange as the sun rises. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast. Then begin trekking toward Tadapani (2,590m) through dense rhododendron forest — approximately 4-5 hours of trekking with some steep sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Tadapani and check into a teahouse. Tadapani offers excellent close-up views of Annapurna South and Machapuchare. Rest your legs and enjoy the peaceful forest setting. Short optional walk to nearby viewpoints.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse. The forest around Tadapani is home to Himalayan wildlife including langur monkeys and various bird species — keep an eye out at dusk. Warm dinner and early bedtime.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes and hot lemon tea at Ghorepani teahouse (~NPR 350-450)
meals.lunch: Snack bar or light lunch at a trail-side teahouse between Ghorepani and Tadapani (~NPR 300-400)
meals.dinner: Vegetable dal bhat or pasta at Tadapani teahouse (~NPR 450-550)

day_by_day.notes: The Poon Hill sunrise is non-negotiable — set multiple alarms. The trail from Ghorepani to Tadapani passes through one of Nepal's most beautiful rhododendron forests, which will be lush and green in October. Carry a warm layer for the early morning hike.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani down to Chomrong (2,170m) — approximately 4-5 hours through terraced farmland and forest. Chomrong is a large, well-established Gurung village and the last major settlement before entering the Annapurna Sanctuary. Enjoy spectacular views of Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machapuchare throughout the descent and ascent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chomrong and check in to a teahouse. Explore the village — visit the local gompa (monastery) and enjoy the views of the Modi Khola gorge far below. The village has a checkpoint where your ACAP permit will be checked. Rest and prepare for the higher altitude days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset views from Chomrong — the village sits on a ridge with panoramic mountain views. Chat with locals and other trekkers. The teahouses here are among the most comfortable on the route.

meals.breakfast: Egg and toast with tea at Tadapani (~NPR 300-400)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a teahouse in Sinuwa (midway point) (~NPR 400-500)
meals.dinner: Chomrong teahouse — try the local apple raksi (rice wine) with a hearty dal bhat (~NPR 450-550)

day_by_day.notes: Chomrong has a permit checkpoint — have your ACAP permit and TIMS card ready. This is a good place to stock up on snacks and water purification tablets as prices increase significantly beyond this point. Teahouse rooms ~NPR 300-500.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chomrong down a long stone staircase to the Modi Khola river, then ascend through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Bamboo (2,310m) and continue to Dovan (2,600m). This section enters the Annapurna Sanctuary buffer zone — the landscape becomes increasingly dramatic with towering cliffs and dense forest. Trek duration approximately 4-5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Dovan to Himalaya Hotel (2,900m) — a cluster of teahouses in the forest. The trail follows the Modi Khola river upstream. The environment feels increasingly wild and remote. Look out for waterfalls cascading down the canyon walls.
day_by_day.evening: Settle in at Himalaya Hotel teahouse. Temperatures drop noticeably at this altitude. Gather around the teahouse stove. The sound of the river rushing below creates a peaceful ambiance. Early night for acclimatization.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and honey with tea at Chomrong (~NPR 350-450)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at Bamboo teahouse (~NPR 450-550)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with spinach and lentils at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (~NPR 500-600). Note: prices increase inside the sanctuary.

day_by_day.notes: This section of trail can be affected by landslides after heavy rain — check with teahouse owners about trail conditions. Carry enough cash as there are no ATMs beyond Chomrong. Water from streams must be purified. Altitude sickness can begin to affect some trekkers — go slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel through Hinku Cave (a natural rock overhang used as shelter) to Deurali (3,230m). The forest gives way to more open terrain. On clear October mornings, the walls of the Annapurna Sanctuary begin to reveal themselves — towering snow-capped peaks emerging above the valley. Trek duration ~3-4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Deurali to Machapuchare Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m) — approximately 2-3 more hours. The landscape transforms dramatically as you exit the forest and enter the high alpine zone. Machapuchare (Fishtail Peak, 6,993m) dominates the skyline. MBC sits in a spectacular bowl surrounded by giants. Check in to a teahouse and acclimatize.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the alpenglow on Machapuchare and Annapurna III as the sun sets. The silence and scale of the mountains here is overwhelming. Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol to aid acclimatization. Sleep early.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes and hot ginger tea at Himalaya Hotel (~NPR 400-500)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup (excellent for altitude) and bread at Deurali (~NPR 500-600)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at MBC teahouse (~NPR 600-700). Garlic soup again recommended for altitude.

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness is a real concern above 3,000m. Symptoms include headache, nausea, and dizziness. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Drink 3-4 liters of water daily. Garlic soup is a trekker favorite believed to help with acclimatization. Temperatures at MBC can drop below freezing at night — use your sleeping bag liner.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at 4:00 AM for the short 45-minute hike from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, 4,130m). Arrive at ABC for one of the most extraordinary sunrises on Earth — a 360-degree amphitheater of Himalayan giants including Annapurna I (8,091m, the world's 10th highest), Annapurna South, Annapurna III, Gangapurna, Hiunchuli, and Machapuchare. Stand in the sacred cirque and absorb the magnitude of the moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning at ABC exploring the base camp area, taking photos, and soaking in the views. After lunch, begin the descent back toward MBC and continue down to Deurali or Himalaya Hotel to sleep at a lower, safer altitude (~3-4 hours descent).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at lower teahouse (Himalaya Hotel or Dovan). Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers. The descent will feel much easier on the lungs. Enjoy a warm meal and rest well.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and biscuits before the pre-dawn hike, then full breakfast at ABC — eggs and toast (~NPR 600-700)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or dal bhat at ABC teahouse (~NPR 650-750)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Himalaya Hotel or Dovan teahouse (~NPR 500-600)

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the entire trip — reaching ABC at 4,130m. In October, the weather is typically stable and clear. However, always check with teahouse owners about morning cloud cover. The descent from ABC to lower altitude is essential for safety — do not sleep at ABC unless you are well acclimatized. This is a long and physically demanding day.

day_by_day.morning: Continue the descent from the lower teahouse through the bamboo and rhododendron forest back toward Chomrong. The descent retraces your steps but feels entirely different — you can move faster and enjoy the scenery with fresh eyes. Trek from Himalaya Hotel/Dovan back to Bamboo (~2-3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descending from Bamboo back up the stone staircase to Chomrong (2,170m) — approximately 2-3 more hours. Arrive in Chomrong and check in to a teahouse. Your legs will feel the long descent — stretch and rest. Enjoy hot lemon tea on the teahouse terrace with mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the successful ABC summit push in Chomrong. The village has slightly better facilities — some teahouses have hot showers (NPR 200-300 extra). Treat yourself to a warm shower after days on the trail.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at lower teahouse (~NPR 400-500)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Bamboo teahouse (~NPR 450-550)
meals.dinner: Chomrong teahouse — spring rolls, dal bhat, or pasta (~NPR 450-550)

day_by_day.notes: Knees will feel the long descents — use trekking poles and take rest breaks. The stone staircases are hard on joints. Anti-inflammatory tablets (ibuprofen) can help if needed. Check your gear and repack for the remaining trek days.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chomrong back toward Ghorepani via a different route — head toward Sinuwa and then take the trail toward Chhomrong Khola and up toward the ridge. Alternatively, take the direct route back through Tadapani to Ghorepani. This section passes through beautiful terraced villages and offers different perspectives on the Annapurna range. Trek ~5-6 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Ghorepani (2,860m). Rest at a teahouse. If energy allows, take a short walk to the viewpoint above the village for afternoon mountain views. The rhododendron forest glows beautifully in the October afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the high mountains. Enjoy a quiet dinner and reflect on the incredible journey of the past week. The Annapurna peaks glow in the last light of day. Pack carefully for the descent to Nayapul tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Egg and toast with tea at Chomrong (~NPR 350-450)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a trail teahouse (~NPR 400-500)
meals.dinner: Ghorepani teahouse — dal bhat or fried noodles with vegetables (~NPR 450-550)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long trekking day — start early (7:00 AM). The trail between Chomrong and Ghorepani via Tadapani is well-marked but involves significant elevation changes. Carry enough water and snacks. October afternoons can bring light cloud cover — mornings offer the best views.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the mountains — one last optional sunrise hike to Poon Hill if you missed it earlier, or simply enjoy the mountain views from the teahouse terrace. After breakfast, begin the descent from Ghorepani through Ulleri and down the famous stone staircase to Tikhedhunga and then to Nayapul. Trek duration ~4-5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul and board a local bus or shared jeep back to Pokhara (~1.5-2 hours, NPR 200-300). Arrive in Pokhara by early afternoon. Check back in to a Lakeside guesthouse. Head straight for a hot shower and change of clothes. Treat yourself to a proper café meal in Pokhara — you've earned it.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the completion of your Annapurna trek with a lakeside dinner. Watch the sunset over Phewa Lake with the Annapurna and Machapuchare peaks reflecting in the water. Visit a rooftop bar for a well-deserved cold Everest beer (NPR 400-500).

meals.breakfast: Last mountain breakfast — porridge and tea at Ghorepani (~NPR 350-450)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Tikhedhunga or snack at Nayapul before the bus (~NPR 350-450)
meals.dinner: Celebrate at a Lakeside Pokhara restaurant — try a proper Nepali thali or a pizza/pasta treat (~NPR 600-800). Splurge slightly — you've completed the trek!

day_by_day.notes: The descent from Ghorepani to Nayapul is hard on the knees — take it slowly. Buses from Nayapul to Pokhara run frequently. Upon returning to Pokhara, visit a pharmacy if you have any blisters or muscle soreness needing attention. Return any rented gear to the shop.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed final morning in Pokhara. Wake up naturally — no early alarms! Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at a Lakeside café. Take a final peaceful rowboat ride on Phewa Lake to say goodbye to the Annapurna peaks. Visit the Bindhyabasini Temple — one of Pokhara's oldest and most important Hindu temples — for a cultural farewell.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse the Lakeside market for last-minute souvenirs — handmade thangka paintings, pashmina scarves, Tibetan singing bowls, and trekking patches are all budget-friendly options (NPR 200-1500). Pack your bags and check out of the guesthouse. Board the afternoon tourist bus or public bus back to Kathmandu (~8 hours, NPR 500-800) for an overnight journey, or book a flight if budget allows (NPR 6,000-9,000 one way, ~30 minutes).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Kathmandu by evening (if taking the bus). Check in to a Thamel guesthouse for one final night. Stroll through Thamel for a final dinner and last-minute shopping. Reflect on an incredible 14-day Annapurna adventure.

meals.breakfast: Lakeside café — full breakfast with eggs, toast, fresh juice, and coffee (~NPR 400-600). Treat yourself on the last day!
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Pokhara before departure — momo and lassi (~NPR 350-450)
meals.dinner: Thamel restaurant in Kathmandu — final Nepali dal bhat or try a farewell splurge at a slightly nicer restaurant (~NPR 600-900)

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight departs from Kathmandu, ensure you arrive the night before or very early morning to allow time for airport transit. Keep some NPR for airport taxes and last-minute expenses. The Pokhara-to-Kathmandu bus journey is scenic but long — book a tourist bus for more comfort (NPR 800 vs NPR 500 for local). Carry your trekking permits and any receipts as souvenirs of your incredible Annapurna journey.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Pokhara/Kathmandu airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Annapurna region. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby village to get acquainted with the surroundings and altitude
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the resort terrace, enjoy the Annapurna mountain views at sunset, and attend a brief trek orientation/briefing session if offered by the resort. Stroll through the local market street nearby

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or dal bhat at a local teahouse near the resort upon arrival
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — try the Nepali thali set menu (approx. NPR 600–900)

day_by_day.notes: Prioritize hydration and rest on arrival day. Begin altitude acclimatization — avoid strenuous activity. Keep luggage light for the transfer. Exchange currency at the airport or ask the resort about local exchange options.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle acclimatization hike to a nearby viewpoint (e.g., Sarangkot or local ridge trail) for panoramic Annapurna and Machapuchare views. Depart by 7:00 AM to catch the golden morning light on the peaks
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort by midday. Visit the Pokhara lakeside area (Phewa Lake) — take a short rowboat ride on the lake with views of the Annapurna range reflecting on the water
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Lakeside (Baidam) area on foot. Browse local trekking gear shops and handicraft stalls. Watch sunset over Phewa Lake

meals.breakfast: Porridge, eggs, and Nepali tea at the resort or a local bakery café (approx. NPR 300–500)
meals.lunch: Lakeside café lunch — try momos (dumplings) and lemon tea at a mid-range café (approx. NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Lakeside restaurant — try butter chicken or mixed grill with local bread (approx. NPR 700–1000)

day_by_day.notes: This is still an acclimatization day. Keep the hike under 3 hours and avoid going above 1,500m elevation gain. Carry at least 2 liters of water.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the classic Annapurna Circuit or Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trail approach — take a jeep or local bus to Nayapul (1,070m) and start trekking toward Tikhedhunga or Ulleri. Trek through terraced rice fields and rhododendron forests
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking uphill through stone-paved trails, passing traditional Gurung and Magar villages. Arrive at Ulleri (1,960m) or Tikhedhunga — rest and explore the village
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a mid-range teahouse/lodge. Socialize with fellow trekkers and enjoy the mountain village atmosphere. Watch the alpenglow on the Annapurna South face

meals.breakfast: Toast, eggs, and tea at the resort before departure (approx. NPR 300–400)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a trail teahouse in Birethanti or Hile (approx. NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat (unlimited refills) at the teahouse lodge — the trekker's staple meal (approx. NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Carry your TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) — ensure these are arranged before departure. Pack rain gear as October afternoons can bring brief showers. Wear layered clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning trek from Ulleri toward Ghorepani (2,860m), ascending through magnificent rhododendron and oak forests. The trail offers increasingly dramatic mountain views as you gain altitude
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghorepani by early afternoon. Check into a mid-range teahouse. Rest and acclimatize. Take a short exploratory walk around the village and visit the local gompa (Buddhist monastery)
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk or short hike to nearby ridge for Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South views. Return to teahouse for a warm evening with fellow trekkers around a communal dining room fire

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and Nepali milk tea at the teahouse (approx. NPR 300–450)
meals.lunch: Pasta or fried rice with vegetables at a trail teahouse midway (approx. NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Garlic soup (altitude remedy) followed by dal bhat or vegetable curry at the Ghorepani teahouse (approx. NPR 500–750)

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is highly recommended at altitude — it helps with acclimatization. Stay well hydrated. The climb from Ulleri to Ghorepani involves significant elevation gain — take it slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up (4:30 AM) and 45-minute hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) for the most iconic Himalayan sunrise in Nepal — 360-degree views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, II, III, IV, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for breakfast, then continue trekking toward Tadapani (2,630m) through dense rhododendron forests. Arrive and settle in by mid-afternoon
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the Tadapani teahouse with mountain views. Write in your travel journal, review photos, and enjoy the peaceful high-altitude village atmosphere as stars emerge

meals.breakfast: Hot chocolate and apple pancakes at Ghorepani after the Poon Hill sunrise (approx. NPR 350–500)
meals.lunch: Cheese sandwich and lemon tea at a trail stop between Ghorepani and Tadapani (approx. NPR 350–500)
meals.dinner: Vegetable stew and rice, or pasta with tomato sauce at the Tadapani teahouse (approx. NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the highlight of many Annapurna treks — arrive early to secure a good viewing spot. Bring a headlamp and warm layers as pre-dawn temperatures at 3,210m can drop to 0–5°C in October.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani toward Chhomrong (2,170m), descending through forests and crossing suspension bridges over the Modi Khola river. Enjoy views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong, a large Gurung village with well-established teahouses and lodges. Explore the village, visit the local school, and enjoy the stunning terrace views of Annapurna South
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from Chhomrong's elevated terraces are spectacular. Enjoy a warm shower (available at most Chhomrong lodges) and a relaxed evening. This is one of the last reliable shower stops before ABC

meals.breakfast: Muesli with yogurt and honey, and ginger tea at Tadapani teahouse (approx. NPR 350–500)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or fried noodles at a teahouse in Sinuwa or on the trail (approx. NPR 450–600)
meals.dinner: Apple pie (Chhomrong is famous for it!) and a hearty dinner of dal bhat or pizza at a lodge (approx. NPR 600–850)

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong is a key gateway village to Annapurna Base Camp. Stock up on snacks, water purification tablets, and any trekking supplies here. Lodges fill up in October peak season — ask your resort to pre-book if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong descending to Sinuwa (2,360m) and then ascending through bamboo and rhododendron forests toward Dovan (2,600m). The trail enters the Annapurna Sanctuary corridor
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) to Deurali (3,230m) if energy allows, or rest at Himalaya Hotel. The landscape becomes increasingly dramatic with towering canyon walls on either side
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a teahouse at Deurali or Himalaya Hotel. The atmosphere becomes noticeably wilder and more remote. Enjoy a quiet evening with stunning canyon and peak views

meals.breakfast: Eggs on toast and Nepali tea at Chhomrong lodge (approx. NPR 350–500)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or dal bhat at Sinuwa or Bamboo teahouse (approx. NPR 450–600)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry with rice and garlic soup at the teahouse (approx. NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: The trail between Chhomrong and Deurali can be prone to landslides and leeches in wet conditions. Wear gaiters. Teahouse options become more limited beyond this point — expect basic but comfortable accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Final push to Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m) — depart Deurali early morning and trek through Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m). The landscape opens into a dramatic glacial amphitheater surrounded by giants
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Annapurna Base Camp — a truly awe-inspiring moment surrounded by Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Hiunchuli, and Machapuchare. Explore the base camp area, take photos, and soak in the atmosphere
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset paint the surrounding peaks in shades of gold, orange, and pink from base camp. This is one of the most spectacular mountain evenings in the world. Stay overnight at ABC teahouse

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and tea at Deurali before the final push (approx. NPR 400–550)
meals.lunch: Light snacks, energy bars, and hot drinks at MBC (approx. NPR 300–400)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dal bhat dinner at ABC teahouse — you've made it! (approx. NPR 600–800)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness is a real risk at 4,130m. Know the symptoms: severe headache, nausea, disorientation, loss of coordination. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Drink 3–4 liters of water. Sleep with a warm sleeping bag — October nights at ABC can reach -10°C to -15°C.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up to witness the extraordinary ABC sunrise — Annapurna I glows a brilliant orange-gold as the first rays hit the summit. One of the most photographed moments in Himalayan trekking
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC back toward Chhomrong, retracing the trail through MBC, Deurali, and Himalaya Hotel. Descending is faster and easier on the lungs
day_by_day.evening: Reach Bamboo or Sinuwa teahouse by evening. Celebrate the successful ABC summit with fellow trekkers. The lower altitude will already feel noticeably easier to breathe

meals.breakfast: Hot chocolate and toast at ABC after sunrise (approx. NPR 400–550)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Himalaya Hotel or Dovan on the descent (approx. NPR 450–600)
meals.dinner: Noodle soup and vegetable curry at Bamboo or Sinuwa teahouse (approx. NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Descending quickly after ABC is recommended to avoid prolonged altitude exposure. Your knees will feel the descent — use trekking poles if available. Pace yourself on the steep sections.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Sinuwa/Bamboo back through Chhomrong and onward toward Jhinu Danda (1,780m), a small village famous for its natural hot springs on the Modi Khola riverbank
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jhinu Danda and descend the steep stone steps to the natural hot spring pools by the river. Soak your tired trekking muscles in the geothermally heated pools — an absolute highlight after days of trekking
day_by_day.evening: Return up to Jhinu Danda village for the night. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the teahouse, reflecting on the incredible journey to ABC. The worst of the physical exertion is now behind you

meals.breakfast: Porridge and eggs at Chhomrong before the final descent leg (approx. NPR 350–500)
meals.lunch: Snacks and fruit at a trail stop (approx. NPR 200–350)
meals.dinner: Grilled chicken or dal bhat with fresh vegetables at Jhinu Danda teahouse (approx. NPR 550–750)

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs are a beloved trekker tradition — bring a towel and swimwear. The pools are open during daylight hours. The descent from Chhomrong to Jhinu involves steep stone steps — take your time to protect your knees.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Jhinu Danda back to Nayapul via Kimche and the Modi Khola valley. The trail winds through terraced farmland, traditional villages, and subtropical forest — a beautiful final day of trekking
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Nayapul and take a local jeep or bus back to Pokhara. Return to the Aegean Bliss Resort, check back in, enjoy a hot shower, and rest your legs. Celebrate the completion of the Annapurna trek
day_by_day.evening: Lakeside Pokhara evening — enjoy a well-deserved sit-down dinner at a proper restaurant. Browse the lively Lakeside market, enjoy live Nepali folk music at a local venue

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast at Jhinu Danda teahouse (approx. NPR 350–500)
meals.lunch: Final trail dal bhat or noodles at a teahouse near Nayapul (approx. NPR 400–550)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a Lakeside Pokhara restaurant — try the Nepali set dinner with local wine or Everest beer (approx. NPR 800–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: You've completed one of the world's most iconic treks! Take time to rest and recover. Wash and dry your trekking gear. Consider a massage at one of Pokhara's many affordable massage centers (approx. NPR 1,000–1,500 for a full-body session).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Optional: visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara — a world-class museum dedicated to the Himalayas, its mountains, and the people who climb them
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Pokhara's natural attractions: visit Davis Falls (Devi's Fall), a dramatic underground waterfall, and the adjacent Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave. Then visit the Tibetan Refugee Camp at Tashiling for cultural insight and handcraft shopping
day_by_day.evening: Sunset paragliding flight over Pokhara and the Annapurna range from Sarangkot (optional, approx. USD 80–100 with a certified operator) — or watch the sunset from Sarangkot viewpoint for free

meals.breakfast: Full Western or Nepali breakfast at the resort — treat yourself after the trek (approx. NPR 500–700)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Lakeside café — try the famous Pokhara apple pie and coffee (approx. NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Lakeside restaurant dinner — try the Himalayan trout (locally farmed) with garlic butter and roasted vegetables (approx. NPR 800–1,100)

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding in Pokhara is world-class and very safe with certified operators. October offers excellent flying conditions with clear skies. Book in the morning for an afternoon or sunset flight. The International Mountain Museum is open 9 AM–5 PM (closed Tuesdays).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat ride on Phewa Lake to the Tal Barahi Temple, a small island temple sacred to the Hindu goddess Barahi. The still morning lake with Annapurna reflections is breathtaking
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike or take a taxi to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) on the southern ridge above Phewa Lake — a stunning white Buddhist stupa with panoramic views of the lake and Annapurna range. Explore the surrounding forest trails
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Pokhara — enjoy a sunset cocktail at a Lakeside rooftop bar, then a farewell dinner. Visit the Baidam night market for last-minute souvenirs: Thangka paintings, singing bowls, yak wool scarves, and trekking mementos

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with honey and butter and butter tea at a lakeside café (approx. NPR 350–500)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near the World Peace Pagoda — buy local snacks and fruit from a village vendor (approx. NPR 300–450)
meals.dinner: Farewell Pokhara dinner — splurge slightly on a rooftop restaurant with Annapurna views. Try the mixed Nepali-Continental menu (approx. NPR 900–1,400)

day_by_day.notes: The boat ride to Tal Barahi Temple costs approx. NPR 500–700 for a round trip. Rowing yourself is an option for the adventurous. The World Peace Pagoda hike takes about 45 minutes from the lakeside — wear sturdy shoes as the path can be slippery.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort with Annapurna views. Pack, check out, and take a final walk along the Phewa Lake promenade. Visit any remaining shops for last-minute gifts
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Pokhara Airport or Kathmandu (by flight or tourist bus — approx. 6–7 hours by bus, 25 minutes by flight). If time permits in Kathmandu, visit Pashupatinath Temple or Boudhanath Stupa before your onward flight
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations — check in for flight LH return journey. Reflect on an extraordinary 14 days in the Annapurna region of Nepal

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full spread with eggs, toast, fruit, and Nepali tea (approx. NPR 500–700)
meals.lunch: Airport café or Kathmandu restaurant lunch — try one last dal bhat or momos (approx. NPR 400–700)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. Declare any trekking permits and cultural artifacts at customs if required. Nepal's departure tax is typically included in international flight tickets.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer from Pokhara Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Annapurna region. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome refreshment and a personal orientation tour of the resort grounds. Settle into your Beachfront suite overlooking the lakeside or mountain vista. Rest and acclimatize to the altitude.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the resort's premium terrace or lakeside deck with panoramic Annapurna and Machapuchare (Fishtail) mountain views. Light welcome cocktails arranged by the concierge.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant — curated Nepali tasting menu featuring dal bhat royale, slow-cooked lamb sekuwa, and saffron kheer dessert, paired with premium Himalayan herbal teas and imported wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrive well-hydrated. The resort concierge will brief you on the 14-day itinerary. Altitude in Pokhara is approximately 820m — no acclimatization concerns on Day 1. Unpack and rest early to prepare for full days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided sunrise boat ride on Phewa Lake with unobstructed views of the Annapurna range reflected on the water. Visit the iconic Tal Barahi Temple on the lake island via wooden rowboat. Guided by a certified naturalist who explains local flora, fauna, and Himalayan geography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided nature walk through the Pokhara lakeside trail to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) via a scenic forest path. Enjoy 360-degree panoramic views of the Annapurna massif, Dhaulagiri, and Pokhara valley from the hilltop stupa. Private photography session arranged with a professional mountain photographer.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Lakeside (Baidam) with a private guide. Explore curated artisan boutiques for premium Pashmina, Thangka paintings, and handcrafted jewelry. Return to resort for a traditional Nepali cultural performance arranged exclusively for guests.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort featuring fresh Himalayan fruits, eggs Benedict, Nepali-style sel roti with honey, and freshly brewed Ilam estate tea
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket on the hillside near the Peace Pagoda — artisan sandwiches, local cheese, seasonal fruits, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-rated lakeside restaurant in Pokhara — Moosehead Restaurant or Caffe Concerto — featuring wood-fired continental cuisine and premium wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Bring sunscreen and a light jacket for the hilltop pagoda. The boat ride is best enjoyed before 8:00 AM for calm waters and optimal mountain reflections.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private transfer to Sarangkot Hill (1,592m). Witness one of Nepal's most spectacular sunrises over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. A premium hot beverage station (coffee, herbal teas, hot chocolate) will be set up at the viewpoint by your private team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional premium paragliding experience over Pokhara valley with a certified tandem pilot — soaring above Phewa Lake and the Annapurna foothills for approximately 30 minutes. Alternatively, guided hike along the Sarangkot ridge trail through rhododendron and pine forests with a naturalist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxation evening at the resort. Indulge in a 90-minute Himalayan Healing Spa treatment — Tibetan hot stone massage with locally sourced herbal oils. Followed by private rooftop stargazing session with a telescope arranged by the resort.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light snack box (croissants, energy bars, thermos of coffee) at Sarangkot; full hot breakfast served upon return to the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at the resort's pool-side restaurant — grilled Himalayan trout, quinoa salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: In-room private dining experience — chef's special four-course Nepali-continental fusion menu served on your beachfront terrace under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Departure for Sarangkot must be by 5:00 AM. Bring a warm fleece jacket — temperatures at the viewpoint can drop to 8–10°C before sunrise. Paragliding is weather-dependent; the resort will confirm availability the evening prior.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day guided trek to Poon Hill (3,210m) begins — Day 1 of 2. Private 4WD transfer to Nayapul (1,070m), the trail gateway. Begin trekking through Birethanti village and along the Modi Khola river valley. Trek through terraced farmland, subtropical forest, and traditional Gurung villages to Tikhedhunga.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue ascending through stone-stepped trails to Ulleri (1,960m), one of the most iconic staircase climbs in Nepal. Arrive at Ghorepani (2,860m) by late afternoon. Check in to a pre-booked premium teahouse or lodge — the best available in Ghorepani with private rooms and en-suite facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ghorepani village, a classic Annapurna Circuit waypoint. Interact with local Magar and Gurung communities. Warm up by the lodge fireplace with locally brewed tongba (millet beer) or butter tea.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast at the resort before departure — eggs, toast, porridge, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch at a scenic riverside rest stop near Tikhedhunga — wraps, energy bars, local cheese, and fruit
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the premium Ghorepani lodge — vegetable curry, dal bhat, and apple pie with cinnamon cream

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 12–14 km, 6–7 hours. Difficulty: moderate to strenuous due to the Ulleri stone staircase. Trekking poles strongly recommended. A certified, licensed TIMS-registered guide and private porter will accompany you throughout. TIMS card and ACAP permit arranged in advance by the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn start (4:30 AM) for the iconic Poon Hill sunrise hike (45–60 minutes from Ghorepani). Stand at 3,210m and witness a breathtaking 360-degree panorama of over 20 Himalayan peaks including Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna South, Annapurna I (8,091m), and Machapuchare. Sunrise photography with your private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for breakfast, then trek onward through rhododendron forests (one of Asia's largest rhododendron forests) to Tadapani (2,630m). The trail offers exceptional birdwatching opportunities — Himalayan monals, pheasants, and eagles are frequently spotted.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Tadapani in a premium lodge. Enjoy the serene mountain ambiance, evening mist rolling through the forest, and a spectacular mountain backdrop. Early rest to prepare for the descent.

meals.breakfast: Light snack at Poon Hill summit (thermos of hot tea, energy bites); full cooked breakfast at Ghorepani lodge upon return
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at a teahouse en route to Tadapani — noodle soup, fried rice, and ginger lemon honey tea
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tadapani lodge — garlic soup, vegetable momos, dal bhat, and chocolate brownie

day_by_day.notes: Temperature at Poon Hill before sunrise can be 0–5°C — bring a down jacket, gloves, and a head torch. This is the highlight of the Annapurna foothills experience. Trek distance today: approximately 10 km, 5–6 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani through dense rhododendron and oak forests descending to Ghandruk (1,940m), one of the largest and most picturesque Gurung villages in Nepal. Arrive mid-morning and explore the village's traditional stone-paved lanes, ancient water mills, and the Gurung Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Gurung Museum for an immersive cultural experience — learn about Gurung history, traditional costumes, shamanic practices, and the legendary Gurkha warrior heritage. Enjoy a private cultural interaction with a local Gurung family, including a demonstration of traditional weaving and cooking.
day_by_day.evening: Private 4WD vehicle picks up from Ghandruk for the scenic drive back to Pokhara. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Unwind with a post-trek recovery massage at the resort spa — deep tissue or Ayurvedic oil treatment.

meals.breakfast: Cooked breakfast at Tadapani lodge — porridge, eggs, toast, and black tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium teahouse in Ghandruk — fresh trout, vegetable curry, and local millet bread
meals.dinner: Celebratory post-trek dinner at the resort — prime Himalayan lamb chops, roasted seasonal vegetables, and a premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 6 km, 3–4 hours. Ghandruk is a must-visit for cultural immersion. The drive from Ghandruk to Pokhara takes approximately 1.5–2 hours. Tip your guide and porter generously — it is customary and deeply appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Optional gentle yoga session on the lakeside deck led by a certified Himalayan yoga instructor at sunrise. Enjoy the resort's premium wellness facilities — infinity pool, steam room, and meditation garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided excursion to the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara — one of the world's finest mountaineering museums. Explore exhibits on Himalayan geology, legendary expeditions (including the first Annapurna summit by Maurice Herzog in 1950), climbing equipment through the ages, and ethnic mountain cultures.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's premium bar. Followed by a private cooking class with the resort's head chef — learn to prepare authentic Nepali dishes including dal bhat, gundruk soup, and sel roti. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: À la carte resort breakfast — eggs your way, smoked salmon bagel, fresh fruit platter, and specialty Himalayan coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's poolside café — Caesar salad, avocado toast, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the cooking class, supplemented by the chef's premium additions — served on the resort terrace

day_by_day.notes: A rest day is essential after three consecutive trekking days. The International Mountain Museum is approximately 20 minutes from the resort by private car. Museum entry fee included in the resort's concierge arrangement.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter scenic flight over the Annapurna Sanctuary and Base Camp (4,130m). Fly over the Modi Khola gorge, the dramatic glacier-carved Annapurna Sanctuary, and land at Annapurna Base Camp for a 30-minute on-ground experience surrounded by towering 7,000–8,000m peaks. An unparalleled, once-in-a-lifetime Himalayan experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Pokhara by helicopter. Afternoon at leisure — explore the Bindabasini Temple (one of Pokhara's most sacred Hindu temples) and the old Pokhara Bazaar with a private guide. Browse traditional handicrafts, Tibetan carpets, and locally made goods.
day_by_day.evening: Premium dinner reservation at one of Pokhara's finest restaurants — Caffe Concerto or Moosehead — with a curated menu and live acoustic Nepali folk music performance.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the helicopter flight — continental spread with fresh pastries, fruits, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic box enjoyed at Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m) — a truly extraordinary high-altitude dining experience
meals.dinner: Four-course fine dining at a top Pokhara restaurant — appetizer, soup, main course (Himalayan trout or lamb), and dessert with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter flight is entirely weather-dependent and may be rescheduled. Flight duration: approximately 45–60 minutes each way. Warm, windproof clothing is mandatory at ABC (temperatures can be -5°C to 5°C). This is the premium highlight of the entire trip — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided nature hike to the Davis Falls (Patale Chhango) and Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave — a dramatic underground cave system with a sacred Shiva shrine and a natural window overlooking Davis Falls. Guided by a local expert who narrates the geological and cultural significance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seti River Gorge viewpoints — witness the powerful Seti Gandaki River carving through narrow limestone gorges, completely hidden underground in sections. Photography session at the multiple viewpoints. Continue to the Tibetan Refugee Camp at Tashiling for an insightful cultural visit — observe traditional carpet weaving and purchase authentic handmade Tibetan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the resort's beachfront. Private bonfire arranged on the lakeside with s'mores, warm drinks, and ambient Himalayan folk music. A relaxed, intimate evening under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full resort buffet breakfast with live egg station, fresh Himalayan honey, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Pokhara restaurant near the Tibetan Camp — Tibetan thukpa noodle soup, momos, and butter tea
meals.dinner: Lakeside BBQ dinner at the resort — marinated Himalayan meats, grilled vegetables, naan bread, and premium cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The Tibetan Refugee Camp visit is a deeply moving cultural experience. Purchasing handmade carpets or goods directly supports the community. Wear comfortable walking shoes — some uneven terrain around the gorge viewpoints.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day guided trek to Australian Camp and Dhampus — Day 1. Private 4WD transfer to Phedi (1,130m). Trek uphill through terraced farmland and Gurung villages to Australian Camp (2,060m), a popular viewpoint with sweeping Annapurna range vistas. Morning tea and snacks at the camp.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Australian Camp along the ridge trail to Dhampus village (1,650m), one of the most scenic and accessible villages in the Annapurna foothills. Explore the traditional Gurung stone houses, interact with locals, and enjoy unobstructed views of Machapuchare.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at a premium lodge in Dhampus. Enjoy the village's peaceful atmosphere, local hospitality, and a spectacular mountain sunset. Evening bonfire at the lodge with fellow trekkers and local guides.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — full hot breakfast with all accompaniments
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at Australian Camp — sandwiches, local snacks, fresh fruit, and hot tea
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dhampus lodge — freshly prepared dal bhat, vegetable curry, and homemade apple pie

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 8–10 km, 4–5 hours. Difficulty: moderate. This trek offers some of the best accessible Annapurna views without the multi-day commitment. A certified guide and porter are included.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise from Dhampus with spectacular golden light illuminating the Annapurna South and Machapuchare peaks. Morning photography walk around the village with your guide. Visit local homes for a traditional Gurung breakfast experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek back down to Phedi through alternate trail routes passing through dense forest and waterfalls. Private vehicle returns you to Pokhara and the resort. Afternoon check-in, freshen up, and enjoy the resort's infinity pool and spa.
day_by_day.evening: Premium spa evening — choose from a Himalayan hot stone massage, aromatherapy session, or traditional Ayurvedic treatment. Followed by a quiet, intimate dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Gurung breakfast at a local home in Dhampus — buckwheat pancakes, local honey, butter tea, and fresh eggs
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch on the descent — wraps, cheese, fruits, and energy bars
meals.dinner: Elegant resort dinner — slow-cooked Nepali lamb curry, saffron rice, seasonal vegetables, and mango kulfi dessert

day_by_day.notes: The traditional Gurung breakfast is a rare and authentic cultural experience — tipping the host family is appreciated. Trek distance today: approximately 6 km, 2–3 hours descent.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort — sleep in, enjoy a late breakfast, and spend time at the lakeside. Optional kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Phewa Lake arranged by the resort's water sports team. Gentle and relaxing activity with stunning mountain backdrops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided excursion to Begnas Lake and Rupa Lake — twin lakes east of Pokhara, far less visited and exceptionally serene. Enjoy a private boat ride on Begnas Lake surrounded by forested hills and Himalayan peaks. Birdwatching with a naturalist — spot kingfishers, herons, and migratory waterfowl.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell preparation evening. Visit a premium Pashmina and handicraft boutique for last-minute luxury souvenirs — pure cashmere Pashminas, hand-painted Thangkas, silver jewelry, and Singing Bowls. Return to resort for a curated farewell cocktail hour.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late resort breakfast — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lakeside picnic at Begnas Lake — gourmet spread of local cheeses, charcuterie, artisan bread, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Special chef's table dinner at the resort — exclusive seven-course tasting menu celebrating Nepali and Himalayan cuisine, paired with curated wines and spirits

day_by_day.notes: Begnas Lake is approximately 30 minutes from Pokhara — a hidden gem rarely visited by tourists. The chef's table dinner should be pre-booked with the resort at least 24 hours in advance. A truly memorable final full-day dining experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise at Phewa Lake — private boat arranged for one last golden-hour experience on the water with Annapurna reflections. Mindful morning meditation on the boat with the resort's yoga instructor. Return for a leisurely farewell breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack and check out of the resort. Private guided visit to the Bindhyabasini Temple and Old Bazaar for final cultural immersion. Visit a local Thangka painting studio to see artisans at work and acquire a hand-painted piece as a premium keepsake. Private vehicle on standby throughout the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Pokhara Airport or continue to Kathmandu by private vehicle or domestic flight (as per onward travel plans). If staying an additional night in Kathmandu, check in to a premium heritage hotel (Dwarika's Hotel recommended). Farewell dinner in Kathmandu's Thamel district at a top restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full buffet with live stations, champagne, and fresh tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Lakeside café before departure — sandwiches, soup, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Kathmandu at Dwarika's Hotel or Krishnarpan Restaurant — royal Nepali multi-course feast in a heritage setting

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all trekking permits, TIMS cards, and personal documents are collected and safely stored. The resort concierge will arrange all departure logistics including airport transfer, luggage handling, and any last-minute requests.

day_by_day.morning: If in Kathmandu: Morning guided tour of UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Pashupatinath Temple (sacred Hindu cremation ghats), Boudhanath Stupa (one of the world's largest Buddhist stupas), and Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple) with panoramic Kathmandu valley views. A profound and spiritual final morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final shopping in Kathmandu's Thamel district for premium souvenirs — Singing Bowls, Nepali paper products, hand-knotted rugs, and traditional kukri knives. Private transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for departure. Lounge access arranged at the premium airport lounge.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kathmandu. Reflect on an extraordinary 14-day Himalayan journey — from lakeside serenity to high-altitude adventure, cultural immersion to luxury wellness — as you fly home with memories that will last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Kathmandu hotel — full continental and Nepali spread
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a heritage restaurant in Thamel — Nepali thali or continental selection
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport at least 3 hours before international departure — the airport can be busy and security procedures are thorough. Ensure all purchased goods comply with customs regulations. Pashmina, Thangkas, and handicrafts are generally unrestricted. Antiques over 100 years old require special export permits.
